, challenge is to the judgment and order dated 26.08.2021 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Buldhana whereby the learned Sessions Judge dismissed the revision application filed by the applicant challenging the order of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana dated 03.12.2018 rejecting his application for discharge from the crime.
4.

The facts relevant for deciding this application may be stated as follows:
Applicant - Mohd. Sajjad Abdul Khalique Sheikh (hereinafter referred as 'accused No.5') has challenged the order on multiple grounds.
The informant in this case is Muutthukrushnan Shankar Narayanan.
On the date of the report i.e. on 17.03.2012 he was posted as a 'Collector' of District Akola.

In his report, he has stated that on 18.01.2011 he came to know from the newspaper report that the disability certificate was issued in his name by Civil Hospital, Buldhana and thereby he was declared to be 70 % disabled by hearing impairment.
On the basis of his report, crime No. 00 of 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt 2011 was registered at City Kotwali Police Station Akola.
It was sent to the concerned Police station at Buldhana.
At the Buldhana police station the offence was registered.
The investigation was conducted.
The investigation revealed that the accused Nos. 1 to 3 issued the disability certificate.
The accused No. 4 processed the papers submitted for issuance of disability certificate.
The accused No. 5 under his signature issued a residence certificate in the name of the informant.

After completion of the investigation, the police filed chargesheet in a Crime bearing No. 14 of 2011 registered at Buldhana Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
5. The accused Nos. 1 to 5 applied for their discharge by making separate discharge applications in Regular Criminal Case No. 169 of 2018.
The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana allowed the discharge applications made by the accused Nos. 1 to 3.
However, learned Chief Judicial Magistrate rejected the applications made by the accused Nos. 4 and 5.
The accused No. 4 had challenged the order of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana by 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt filing Criminal Application (APL) bearing No. 651 of 2021.
This Court (Coram : Manish Pitale, J) by order dated 23.08.2021 allowed the said application and discharged the accused No. 4, as well, from the said crime.
The accused No. 5 has come before this Court and challenged the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge dismissing his revision.

6. I have heard learned Advocate Mr M. P. Kariya, for the accused No. 5 and learned APP Ms M. H.
Deshmukh for the State.
Perused the record and proceedings.
7. Learned Advocate for the accused No. 5 submitted that there is overwhelming evidence to conclude that this accused No. 5 has not committed any offence.

Learned Advocate submitted that one witness Mr. Mohammad Tausif Mohammad Yusuf has stated that blank certificate with the Mohd. Sajjad Ab. Khalique Sheikh vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Buldhana Tah. ... on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101909059/

sentences.text: In the case of Sanjay Kumar Rai (supra), it is held that the 'discharge' is a valuable right provided to accused.
Trial Court while considering discharge application has to sift through evidence in order to find out whether there are sufficient grounds to try suspect.
The court has to consider broad probabilities, total effect of evidence, documents produced and basic infirmities appearing in the case.
In the remaining decisions, the proposition of law is similar to the one laid down in the case of Sanjay Kumar Rai (supra).

9. Learned APP submitted that the available evidence on record has been properly considered for the limited purpose of deciding the discharge application by the learned Sessions Judge as well as by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana.

Learned 4 2003 Mh.L.J. (5) 792 5 2019 Cri.L.J. 661 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt APP submitted that during the course of investigation the signature on the residence certificate, the admitted signatures of the accused No.5 and his specimen signatures had been sent to the handwriting expert.
Learned APP submitted that there is evidence in the form of the report of the handwriting expert to show that the signature on the residence certificate was made by accused No.5.
Learned APP submitted that the residence certificate issued by accused No. 5 was the foundation and basis for issuance of disability certificate.
Learned APP submitted that the discharge of the accused Nos. 1 to 3, who have issued the disability certificate, will not enure to the benefit of the accused No.5.
Learned APP submitted that in the teeth of the available evidence, the basic requirements of law, to frame the charge against the accused No. 5, have been satisfied.

In order to consider the rival submissions, I have gone through the record and proceedings.
The accused No. 5 is relying upon the statement of prosecution witness Mr. Mohammd Tausif Mohammad Yusuf.
Relying upon his statement, it is submitted that this witness has collected the blank signed certificate 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt from the grandmother of the accused No. 5.
On the basis of this statement, it is contended that except the signature on the said certificate the remaining matter was prepared by other accused persons.
It is to be noted that this defence has been set up by the accused No. 5 on the basis of the statement of the prosecution witnesses Mohammad Tausif Mohammad Yusuf and Samir Khan Nagimuddin Khan.
In my view, on the basis of this defence and particularly keeping in mind the statements of these two witnesses, the accused No. 5 cannot be discharged.

It may not be out of place to mention that the prosecution, in view of the candid statements by witnesses Mohammad Tausif Mohammad Yusuf and Samir Khan Nagimuddin Khan, ought to have made an application to arraigned them as an accused in this case.
Be that as it may, the fact remains that in view of their statements role of the accused No. 5 will not get diluted.

His defence that blank certificate with his signature was taken by the witness and the said blank certificate was filled with relevant matter and used by the person who were master mind in the sting operation is not believable.

It is the case of the prosecution that the sting operation was conducted because the disability 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt certificates were issued from Civil Hospital, Buldhana for the asking without verifying the documents and examining the patient.
The object of the sting operators may be laudable.
However, that cannot take away the responsibility of the accused No. 5.
Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana for the reasons recorded in his order has discharged the Doctors.
Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana observed that the Doctors did not create any false record.

Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Buldhana observed that the Doctors were led by the evidence placed before them which included this residence certificate issued by the accused No. 5 to issue the disability certificate.
Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate further observed that the certificate issued by the accused No. 5 was the foundation for issuance of disability certificate.
11. It is to be noted that the signature on the disputed residence certificate has been matched with the specimen signatures of the accused No. 5.

It is apparent on the face of the record that on the basis of the residence certificate, issued by the accused No. 5, the disability certificate was issued to a fictitious person on 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt 28.12.2010.
The evidence, therefore, clearly indicates that the prime role was played by the accused No. 5 in the entire episode.
In my view, the case of the accused No. 5 is not fit for discharge.
There is ample material on record to prima facie establish the complicity of the accused No. 5 in the commission of the crime.
The material complied in the chargesheet is more than enough to draw a presumption that the accused No. 5 has committed the offence.
On the basis of the material on record the charge deserves to be framed against the accused.

12. In the context of the above factual position it would be necessary to make useful reference to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Tarun Jit Tejpal Vs. State of Goa and Mohd. Sajjad Ab. Khalique Sheikh vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Buldhana Tah. ...

sentences.text: wherein it has been held that appreciation of evidence at the time of framing of the charge or while considering discharge application, is not permissible.

The Court is not permitted 8 (2020) 17 SCC 556 9 (1990) 4 SCC 76 10 (2010) 9 SCC 368 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt to analyse all the material touching the pros and cons, reliability and acceptability of the evidence.

In the case of Tarun Jit Tejpal (supra), it is held that at the time of consideration of the application for discharge, the Court cannot act as a mouth piece of the prosecution or act as a post office and may sift evidence in order to find out whether or not the allegations made are groundless so as to pass an order of discharge.

It is held that at the stage of consideration of application for discharge, the Court has to proceed with an assumption that the materials brought on record by prosecution are true and evaluate the said materials and documents with a view to find out whether the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offences.
At this stage, the Court is not expected to go deep into the matter and hold that materials would not warrant a conviction.
It is held that what needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not whether a ground for convicting accused has been made out.
It is further held that the law does not permit a mini trial at the stage of deciding the discharge application or at the 32.apl.1103.2021.judge.odt time of framing of charge.
13. In view of the above, I am of the view that law carved out from the above decision is against the accused No. 5.
The acceptance of the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the accused would require appreciation of the evidence touching the merits of the case of the prosecution.
If such exercise is undertaken, at this stage, it will be a sort of a mini trial.
The mini trial is not permitted at the stage of discharge, while considering the discharge application.
As such, the application stands dismissed.
14. The criminal application stands disposed of, accordingly.
15. Rule stands discharged.
No costs.
